page: UpCloud PREMIUM-16xCPU-64GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with 300 GB of local SSD space, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark results show average performance across most standard workloads. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests score in the middle 50% tier, at 1838.78 and 44425.64 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 2685.2 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 147.28 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The server excels in single-threaded gzip compression, achieving a top-tier score of 39.49 GB/sec, and shows strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.14 GB/sec. However, a notable performance tradeoff is observed in LLM text generation using a small 135M model, which registers a poor speed of 9.08 tokens/sec, though prompt processing for the same model remains average at 557.46 tokens/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation, this server offers a balanced resource density for workloads that do not require dedicated, continuous CPU execution. The inclusion of 300 GB of SSD storage and 64 GB of RAM makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for hosting databases, running static web servers, and executing general-purpose application workloads. It is well-suited for database operations, static web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications that benefit from a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio.

The CPU supports advanced vector and cryptographic instructions, including AVX-512 and AES. Performance benchmarks place this server in the average tier for most operations, including a PassMark CPU score of 35388.02 and a static web serving throughput of 21.01 GB/sec, though it achieves top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 39.49 GB/sec. Conversely, LLM text generation for small models is a performance bottleneck. This configuration is best suited for database operations, static web serving, and general-purpose business applications requiring a balanced resource profile.
